title: Household and Income Definitions for the Patient Financial Assistance Program
content:
**Household.** For every tier of the Patient Financial Assistance Program, the household is the applicant, the applicant's spouse or domestic partner, and the dependents claimed on the applicant's federal tax return. Household size counts those people.

**Whose income counts.** Income of a spouse or domestic partner is counted. Income of dependents is not counted.

**Which document sets annual income.** Annual household income is taken from the most recent accepted income document.

| Tier | Household | Spouse or partner income counted | Dependent income counted | Annual income taken from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Financial Assistance 25% Discount | Applicant, spouse or domestic partner, and dependents claimed on the applicant's federal tax return | Yes | No | Most recent accepted income document |
| Financial Assistance 50% Discount | Same definition | Yes | No | Most recent accepted income document |
| Financial Assistance 75% Discount | Same definition | Yes | No | Most recent accepted income document |
| Financial Assistance Full Discount | Same definition | Yes | No | Most recent accepted income document |
| Presumptive Eligibility Full Discount | Same definition | Yes | No | Most recent accepted income document |
| Catastrophic Medical Hardship Adjustment | Same definition | Yes | No | Most recent accepted income document |

## Applying the definitions (hypothetical household)

An applicant lives with a domestic partner and two children; the children are claimed on the applicant's federal tax return, and one of them, aged seventeen, has a part-time job.

- Household size: four (the applicant, the partner and the two claimed children).
- Income counted: the applicant's and the partner's. The seventeen-year-old's wages are not counted, because dependent income is not counted.
- If the household has supplied both a tax return and later pay stubs, annual income is taken from the more recent of the accepted documents.
